claims.text: Multi-principal-element high-entropy alloys can have disordered crystalline random-solid-solution structures.
The alloys targeted by the approach feature significant atomic-mass contrast and lattice distortion.
The proposed predictive approach uses configurational entropy, mass-contrast descriptors, and simulated phonon-density-of-states indicators.
Phonon-density-of-states information is relevant to understanding heat-transfer mechanisms in HEAs.
Changing individual-element concentrations can control the lattice thermal conductivity of HEAs.
Enhanced configurational entropy together with atomic-mass and force-constant differences produces severe lattice distortion.
Chemical disorder in HEAs produces mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Disorder-induced mass and force-constant fluctuations increase phonon scattering and reduce phonon lifetime.
Increased phonon scattering reduces phonon mean free path and lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed descriptors capture disorder-induced lattice perturbations more effectively than traditional averaged-property models.
The proposed model will identify low-phonon-conductivity HEAs more reliably than traditional heuristic predictions.
HEAs selected by the proposed model will have phonon thermal conductivity approximately 20–30% lower than materials selected by conventional methods.
Current prediction models rely mainly on heuristic phase diagrams and averaged thermophysical properties.
Current models do not fully account for chemical-disorder and mass-fluctuation effects in HEAs.
The approach will be most effective in multicomponent systems having large atomic-mass differences and high configurational entropy.
The approach will be less applicable to alloys with nearly identical constituent masses or low configurational disorder.
The quantitative improvement depends on descriptor accuracy and model generalization across HEA compositions.
Inelastic neutron scattering can characterize HEA phonon dynamics and phonon density of states.
Failure of model-selected HEAs to show at least 20% lower phonon thermal conductivity than conventionally selected controls would falsify the hypothesis.
